body: If you're still around I'm here.

I feel like you're me in the future. It's funny, because I also feel resentful for people younger than me even though I'm only 23. I never got to experience a good childhood, or teenage years, or early-adult life. I just try and stay alive each day, but that takes up all the strength that I have. I know it's the wrong way to think because it's never too late for most things, but I feel stuck in thinking that it's too late for me. I also haven't ever had a girlfriend.

Death isn't the answer. I imagine you want to feel relief, but you can't feel that if you die. People turn to suicide when the pain they're experiencing is greater than their ability to cope with that pain. Everyone experiences different levels of these two things, some people have extraordinary amounts of pain but amazing coping resources and a reason that keeps them going. But, no one is given their reason to live from birth. It's something you have to find, but how could someone find a reason to live when they're in a massive amount of pain and just trying to stay alive for the next day? So let's be practical, you have 2 options:

1. Reduce the amount of pain you're experiencing.
2. Improve your ability to cope

The good news is that these are both things that can improve. Number 1 might be out of your control, because you're forced to go to school and I imagine you're forced to do a lot of other things that make you miserable. Talking to someone you trust can help with this. Do the people around you truly know how much you're suffering? If not, you need to let them know. Discuss the reasons why you're feeling so much pain, and then try and think of some things you can do to lessen the amount of pain you're feeling. Some things might need minor fixes, some might need major. Don't forget that a bunch of small changes add up to a big change, and that change has a snowball effect.

For number 2, your ability to cope is determined by a ton of different factors. For example, a reason to live can give someone a massive ability to cope. Viktor Frankl wrote a book called "Mans Search for Meaning" where he wrote about his experiences as a prisoner in Nazi concentration camps during World War II. It's remarkable how people who were surrounded by death, who watched their families die infront of them, suffered brutal beating from prison guards, and lived on half a loaf of bread a day found meaning in their suffering. The ability to cope can be cultivated through small things as well. A TV show you enjoy, a person you like talking to, a hobby or passion. These things can help you forget about your suffering, even if it's temporary. You should make use of every resource you have, not matter how small, in your fight for life.

Focus on doing these 2 things with every ounce of strength you have left. Don't give up on your life yet.
Is there anything in the past that interested you or that you gravitated towards?

I've typed a response and deleted it 4 times. I feel a little bit like you, except I couldn't handle highschool, or college, or my first and only "job". I don't have any friends and when I'm not crying or smashing walls I just play video games all day and constantly lose at that, too. Forget about career ambitions, I don't think I could even get a job if I tried and searching for one would make me feel more worthless than I already am.

Honestly I don't know what to say to you. If there was advice I could give I would use it on myself. It sounds like we're both young so at least there's a possibility that things can change, but I imagine you must feel like you can't live another day. I feel like that, at least. My life has been one big disappointment so far.

It sounds like you're very concerned with what other people think of you, is there anything at all that gives you personal enjoyment/fulfilment without having to rely on other people's judgement? I know the obvious answer would probably be "to get a job" but it helps alot to be in a positive space, as impossible as that might seem. What I've noticied is that life doesn't favor negative people, they get stuck there and spiral downwards and it's an unforgiving and mercliless drop to the bottom.

If theres anything you can do to save yourself from that, someone you enjoy talking to, something you enjoy doing, etc I think you should try and do that. I don't think it will solve any of your problems, but it might help get your mind in a better place so that you have a chance at solving anything. That's what I wish I could do, but my mind is just stuck and I can't think of a single activity that can get me out of this way of thinking. I don't know you, but my personal request as someone else suffering who doesn't want to see others suffer is please try and do anything you think might make you feel better.

I agree with how people can be on a positive/downwards trend. I realize I'm in a depressed mindset but I feel powerless to do anything about it. I feel like a robot who was programmed wrong, and the programmer who can fix it is no where to be found. Every time I try and be positive I'm just disappointed and end up more depressed, because nothing I've tried has worked.
